To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the return on land acquisition was strongly affected by where the land acquisition took place, the return on land‐use development policy was small relative to the land‐acquisition policy, and that the land‐acquisitions policy was the most effective at increasing aggregate exurban forest levels.

(1) the return on municipal land acquisition for conservation was strongly affected, in terms of the quantity of area conserved and the quality of the conserved forest, by the location strategy of land acquisition; (2) the location strategy for land acquisition was more successful in terms of increasing aggregate forest levels, and the quality of conserved forest, than the independent zoning policy and any combination of both; and (3) the zoning policy was more successful at increasing aggregate forest cover, although the effect

the return on land acquisition is highly sensitive to the location strategy used for selecting parcels for conservation and that the location strategy for land acquisition was more influential towards the overall goal of increasing aggregate forest levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of land use planning and management on forest cover and landscape aesthetics.
the effects of land acquisition policies and zoning on exurban forest cover.
the effects of land use policies on forest cover in exurban areas and the development of a GIS‐based ABM to explore and evaluate land use policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the location strategy for land‐acquisition for forest conservation is a more effective policy than zoning policies alone, or any combination of zoning and land acquisition policies, in maximising forest cover.
land acquisition for conservation purposes, when done strategically, can be more effective in increasing forest cover than large lot zoning policies.
a municipality should consider using a location‐based land acquisition strategy in conjunction with a large lot‐size policy to maximise the amount of forest cover in a municipality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
land‐use planning policies are important for forest conservation and should be implemented in a way that is sensitive to the landscape aesthetic quality of the surrounding landscape.
land acquisition for forest cover is a more effective land‐use policy than zoning, and that land acquisition should be targeted towards areas with high landscape aesthetics.

land acquisition policies for forest conservation can be more effective at increasing forest cover than zoning policies, and that land acquisition policies can be more effective if the location strategy is designed with a goal of increasing aggregate forest cover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combined approach of large lot zoning policies with land acquisition for conservation is a more effective way to conserve forest cover than either policy alone.
land‐use development strategies can be evaluated using a spatially explicit ABM, and this evaluation can be used to inform land‐use development policy.
the effects of zoning policies are not always as straightforward as one might expect and can be influenced by the location strategies used for forest conservation land‐acquisition policies.
